headache.explanation: Headaches are classified into tension, migraine, or cluster types. They are often triggered by stress, sleep deprivation, or chemical imbalances.
headache.advice:
• Rest in a dark, quiet room.
• Apply a cold compress to the forehead.
• Check for light sensitivity or nausea.

fever.explanation: A fever is a temporary increase in your body temperature, often due to an illness.
fever.advice:
• Increase water intake.
• Use a lukewarm sponge bath.
• Monitor temperature every 4-6 hours.
• Seek care if fever exceeds 103°F.

cough.explanation: A cough is a reflex to clear irritants from your airways.
cough.advice:
• Inhale steam or use a humidifier.
• Warm herbal tea with honey.
• Avoid environmental smoke.

chest pain.explanation: Chest pain can stem from heart, lung, or digestive issues. Cardiac-related pain often feels like pressure, squeezing, or fullness.
chest pain.advice:
• STOP ALL ACTIVITY.
• If pain radiates to the jaw or left arm, seek emergency help immediately.

stomach ache.explanation: Abdominal discomfort can be caused by indigestion, gas, or conditions like appendicitis.
stomach ache.advice:
• Sip clear liquids; avoid solids.
• Use a heating pad.
• Seek help if pain is in the lower right abdomen.

rash.explanation: Rashes are inflammatory responses of the skin from allergies, infections, or heat.
rash.advice:
• Avoid scratching.
• Use a cool compress.
• Identify any new allergens in your routine.

cold.explanation: The common cold is a viral infection of your nose and throat.
cold.advice:
• Drink warm fluids.
• Get plenty of rest.
• Saltwater gargles help reduce throat inflammation.

diabetes.explanation: Diabetes refers to a group of diseases that affect how your body uses blood sugar.
diabetes.advice:
• Monitor blood glucose levels frequently.
• Maintain a consistent diet low in sugar.
• Check for symptoms of hypo/hyperglycemia.

back pain.explanation: Low back pain can be caused by muscle strain, disc issues, or poor posture.
back pain.advice:
• Apply heat or ice packs.
• Gentle stretching (child's pose).
• Sleep on a medium-firm mattress with a pillow under your knees.

eye strain.explanation: Digital eye strain results from prolonged screen time and poor lighting.
eye strain.advice:
• Follow the 20-20-20 rule (Look 20 feet away every 20 mins for 20 secs).
• Adjust screen brightness and contrast.
• Blink frequently to prevent dryness.

joint pain.explanation: Joint pain can be caused by injury, arthritis, or repetitive stress.
joint pain.advice:
• Use the RICE method (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
• Gentle movement to prevent stiffness.
• Avoid overhead activities for shoulder pain.

anxiety.explanation: Anxiety is a feeling of unease, such as worry or fear, that can be mild or severe.
anxiety.advice:
• Practice deep breathing exercises.
• Limit caffeine and alcohol intake.
• Maintain a regular sleep schedule.

insomnia.explanation: Insomnia is a sleep disorder where people have trouble falling or staying asleep.
insomnia.advice:
• Establish a consistent sleep routine.
• Limit screen time 1 hour before bed.
• Ensure your bedroom is cool and dark.

burnout.explanation: Burnout is a state of emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive stress.
burnout.advice:
• Set clear boundaries at work.
• Prioritize self-care and hobbies.
• Seek support from family or professionals.

nausea.explanation: Nausea is a sensation of unease and discomfort in the stomach with an urge to vomit.
nausea.advice:
• Drink ginger or peppermint tea.
• Eat bland foods (BRAT diet: Banana, Rice, Applesauce, Toast).
• Stay in a ventilated room.

dizziness.explanation: Dizziness is a feeling of faintness, spinning, or lightheadedness, often linked to hydration or inner ear issues.
dizziness.advice:
• Sit or lie down immediately.
• Drink a full glass of water.
• Avoid sudden head movements.

high blood pressure.explanation: Hypertension is a condition where the force of the blood against your artery walls is too high.
high blood pressure.advice:
• Reduce salt and sodium intake.
• Engage in daily aerobic exercise.
• Track readings in a medical diary.

allergies.explanation: Allergies occur when your immune system reacts to a foreign substance (pollen, dust, food).
allergies.advice:
• Avoid known triggers.
• Use an air purifier at home.
• Keep windows closed during high pollen seasons.

toothache.explanation: Toothaches are usually caused by dental decay, infection, or gum disease.
toothache.advice:
• Rinse with warm salt water.
• Avoid very cold or hot foods.
• Use a cold compress on the outside of your cheek.

ear pain.explanation: Ear pain can result from infections, pressure changes, or earwax buildup.
ear pain.advice:
• Do not insert anything into the ear canal.
• Keep the ear dry while showering.
• Use a warm compress behind the ear.

nosebleed.explanation: Nosebleeds (epistaxis) occur when tiny blood vessels in the nose burst from dry air or trauma.
nosebleed.advice:
• Sit upright and lean slightly forward.
• Pinch the soft part of your nose for 10 minutes.
• Apply ice to the bridge of your nose.

constipation.explanation: Constipation is a common condition where bowel movements are infrequent or difficult.
constipation.advice:
• Increase dietary fiber (fruits, vegetables).
• Drink 8-10 glasses of water daily.
• Engage in moderate physical activity.

diarrhea.explanation: Diarrhea is characterized by loose, watery stools and is often caused by viral or bacterial infections.
diarrhea.advice:
• Stay hydrated with electrolytes.
• Eat bland foods (Rice, Toast).
• Avoid dairy and fatty foods.

heartburn.explanation: Heartburn is a burning sensation in the chest caused by stomach acid backflow into the esophagus.
heartburn.advice:
• Eat smaller, more frequent meals.
• Avoid lying down for 3 hours after eating.
• Limit spicy or acidic foods.

muscle cramp.explanation: Muscle cramps are sudden, involuntary contractions caused by dehydration or overuse.
muscle cramp.advice:
• Gently stretch and massage the muscle.
• Stay hydrated and monitor salt intake.
• Apply heat to tense muscles.

knee pain.explanation: Knee pain can result from injury, arthritis, or mechanical issues like a knee cap misalignment.
knee pain.advice:
• Use the RICE method (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation).
• Wear supportive footwear.
• Avoid heavy lifting or squatting.

shoulder pain.explanation: Shoulder pain is often linked to rotator cuff injuries, bursitis, or frozen shoulder.
shoulder pain.advice:
• Rest the affected arm.
• Avoid overhead movements.
• Regular gentle shoulder stretches.

blurry vision.explanation: Blurry vision can be caused by refractive errors, cataracts, or sudden changes in blood sugar.
blurry vision.advice:
• Rest your eyes from all digital screens.
• Check if your glasses need a new prescription.
• Seek immediate help if vision loss is sudden.

dry eyes.explanation: Dry eyes occur when your eyes don't produce enough tears for lubrication.
dry eyes.advice:
• Use lubricating eye drops (artificial tears).
• Avoid direct air from fans or AC.
• Take breaks during computer use.

mouth sores.explanation: Mouth sores (canker sores) are small, painful ulcers inside the mouth.
mouth sores.advice:
• Avoid spicy or acidic foods.
• Rinse with a mix of baking soda and water.
• Use a soft-bristled toothbrush.

hair loss.explanation: Hair loss (alopecia) can be caused by genetics, hormonal changes, or nutrition deficiencies.
hair loss.advice:
• Avoid harsh chemical treatments.
• Maintain a diet rich in iron and protein.
• Reduce stress through meditation.

brittle nails.explanation: Brittle nails often result from lack of moisture or deficiency in vitamins like biotin.
brittle nails.advice:
• Moisturize your hands and nails daily.
• Wear gloves while handling detergents.
• Consider a biotin supplement after consulting a doctor.

night sweats.explanation: Night sweats are episodes of excessive perspiration that occur during sleep.
night sweats.advice:
• Sleep in a cool, ventilated room.
• Wear lightweight cotton pajamas.
• Avoid alcohol or spicy foods before bed.

shortness of breath.explanation: Dyspnea can be caused by lung conditions, heart issues, or high-intensity exercise.
shortness of breath.advice:
• Sit upright and lean forward slightly.
• Practice pursed-lip breathing.
• If persistent and accompanied by pain, seek emergency help.

palpitations.explanation: Heart palpitations are feelings of having a fast-beating, fluttering, or pounding heart.
palpitations.advice:
• Reduce caffeine and nicotine intake.
• Practice relaxation techniques (deep breathing).
• Log when they occur and for how long.

ankle swelling.explanation: Edema in the ankles can be caused by long periods of standing, pregnancy, or circulatory issues.
ankle swelling.advice:
• Elevate your feet above heart level.
• Reduce your daily salt intake.
• Walk around every hour to improve circulation.

frequent urination.explanation: Needing to urinate often can be a sign of diabetes, UTI, or bladder issues.
frequent urination.advice:
• Log your daily fluid intake.
• Avoid bladder irritants like caffeine.
• See a doctor if there is pain or blood.

low energy.explanation: Chronic low energy (lethargy) can be a sign of anemia, poor sleep, or thyroid issues.
low energy.advice:
• Prioritize 7-9 hours of quality sleep.
• Check iron and Vitamin D levels.
• Maintain regular hydration.

tremors.explanation: Tremors are involuntary, rhythmic muscle contractions that cause shaking in one or more body parts.
tremors.advice:
• Reduce intake of stimulants like caffeine.
• Avoid emotional stress and fatigue.
• Log if the shaking happens at rest or during action.

bloating.explanation: Bloating is a feeling of fullness and tightness in the abdomen, often due to gas or digestion issues.
bloating.advice:
• Eat slowly and chew thoroughly.
• Avoid carbonated drinks.
• Light walking after meals can help.

stiff neck.explanation: A stiff neck is often the result of muscles weakening over time from poor posture or sleeping position.
stiff neck.advice:
• Apply heat or ice packs for 15 minutes.
• Gentle neck stretches (ear to shoulder).
• Check your pillow height and support.

heel pain.explanation: Plantar fasciitis is a leading cause of heel pain, involving inflammation of tissue across the bottom of your foot.
heel pain.advice:
• Stretch your calves and arches daily.
• Wear shoes with good arch support.
• Avoid walking barefoot on hard surfaces.

wrist pain.explanation: Wrist pain can result from sudden injury or long-term problems like carpal tunnel or arthritis.
wrist pain.advice:
• Take frequent breaks from typing.
• Use ergonomic keyboards/mice.
• Wear a wrist splint at night for carpal tunnel.

hip pain.explanation: Hip pain can be caused by problems with the joint itself or surrounding ligaments and tendons.
hip pain.advice:
• Avoid sleeping on the painful side.
• Low-impact exercises like swimming.
• Maintain a healthy weight to reduce pressure.

leg cramps.explanation: Leg cramps are sudden contractions usually in the calf, often happening at night.
leg cramps.advice:
• Forcefully stretch the muscle (flex foot up).
• Stay hydrated and check electrolyte levels.
• Take a warm bath before bed.

foot numbness.explanation: Numbness in the feet can be caused by nerve compression or poor circulation.
foot numbness.advice:
• Wear properly fitting shoes.
• Avoid crossing your legs for long periods.
• Check for signs of diabetes or vitamin B12 deficiency.

hand tingling.explanation: Tingling in hands (pins and needles) often points to nerve pressure in the wrist or neck.
hand tingling.advice:
• Check your workstation ergonomics.
• Note if tingling affects specific fingers.
• Avoid repetitive vibrations (power tools).

loss of appetite.explanation: A decreased desire to eat can be linked to stress, infections, or digestive issues.
loss of appetite.advice:
• Eat smaller, colorful meals frequently.
• Stay hydrated even without hunger.
• Monitor any sudden weight changes.

weight loss.explanation: Unexplained weight loss of more than 5% of body weight in 6 months needs medical review.
weight loss.advice:
• Keep a log of your daily caloric intake.
• Check for symptoms of hyperthyroidism.
• Note any changes in appetite or energy.

excessive thirst.explanation: Polydipsia (excessive thirst) can be a sign of high blood sugar or dehydration.
excessive thirst.advice:
• Check your daily water intake versus output.
• Monitor blood glucose if history of diabetes.
• Avoid salty foods and sugary drinks.

dry mouth.explanation: Dry mouth (xerostomia) occurs when salivary glands don't make enough saliva to keep the mouth wet.
dry mouth.advice:
• Sip water frequently throughout the day.
• Chew sugar-free gum to stimulate saliva.
• Avoid mouthwashes containing alcohol.

runny nose.explanation: Rhinorrhea is excess nasal drainage and can be caused by allergies or the common cold.
runny nose.advice:
• Stay hydrated to keep mucus thin.
• Use a saline nasal spray.
• Avoid known allergens like dust or pollen.

sneezing.explanation: Sneezing is a reflex to expel irritants from the nasal cavity.
sneezing.advice:
• Identify and avoid environmental triggers.
• Use an air purifier at home.
• Wash bedding in hot water weekly.

itchy eyes.explanation: Itchy eyes are most commonly a symptom of seasonal or indoor allergies.
itchy eyes.advice:
• Do not rub your eyes; it makes it worse.
• Use a cool compress over closed eyelids.
• Wear sunglasses outdoors to block pollen.

watery eyes.explanation: Excessive tearing can result from irritation, allergies, or blocked tear ducts.
watery eyes.advice:
• Flush eyes with clean water or saline.
• Rest eyes from contact lenses if you use them.
• Check for foreign objects like eyelashes.

acne.explanation: Acne is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells.
acne.advice:
• Wash your face gently twice a day.
• Use non-comedogenic (oil-free) products.
• Avoid picking or squeezing pimples.

dry skin.explanation: Xerosis (dry skin) can be caused by cold weather, hot showers, or low humidity.
dry skin.advice:
• Apply moisturizer while skin is damp.
• Use mild, fragrance-free cleansers.
• Install a humidifier in your home.

oily skin.explanation: Oily skin is the result of overactive sebaceous glands producing too much sebum.
oily skin.advice:
• Use a foaming face wash.
• Apply moisturizer (yes, oily skin needs it too!).
• Avoid touching your face throughout the day.

sunburn.explanation: Sunburn is skin damage caused by ultraviolet (UV) light.
sunburn.advice:
• Take a cool bath or shower.
• Apply aloe vera or moisturizer.
• Drink extra water to prevent dehydration.

insect bite.explanation: Most insect bites cause minor swelling, redness, and itching.
insect bite.advice:
• Wash the area with soap and water.
• Apply a cold pack to reduce swelling.
• Seek help if you have a known allergy or trouble breathing.

bruising.explanation: A bruise forms when blood vessels under the skin tear and leak blood.
bruising.advice:
• Apply ice immediately after injury.
• Elevate the bruised area if possible.
• Seek help if bruising happens easily without injury.

chills.explanation: Chills are your body's way of generating heat when it feels cold, often preceding a fever.
chills.advice:
• Dress in light layers.
• Drink warm fluids like soup or tea.
• Monitor your temperature.

hot flashes.explanation: Hot flashes are sudden feelings of warmth, usually most intense over the face, neck, and chest.
hot flashes.advice:
• Dress in layers that can be removed.
• Keep a cool drink nearby.
• Avoid triggers like caffeine or spicy foods.

dark circles.explanation: Dark circles under the eyes are often caused by fatigue, genetics, or allergies.
dark circles.advice:
• Prioritize 8 hours of sleep.
• Apply a cold compress or tea bags.
• Elevate your head while sleeping.

puffy eyes.explanation: Swelling under the eyes can result from water retention, allergies, or lack of sleep.
puffy eyes.advice:
• Reduce salt intake in your diet.
• Use a chilled jade roller or spoon.
• Rinse eyes with cool water.

bad taste.explanation: A metallic or bitter taste in the mouth can be caused by medications, sinus issues, or dental problems.
bad taste.advice:
• Brush your tongue regularly.
• Floss once a day.
• Stay hydrated to keep saliva flowing.

sneezing fits.explanation: Rapid consecutive sneezing is usually an acute response to an airborne irritant.
sneezing fits.advice:
• Move to a different environment immediately.
• Use a saline rinse to clear your nose.
• Note if it happens near pets or dust.

numb fingers.explanation: Numbness in fingers is often due to circulation issues or nerve endings in the neck or wrist.
numb fingers.advice:
• Shake your hands gently to restore flow.
• Avoid resting your elbows on hard surfaces.
• Check for Raynaud's syndrome if skin turns white.

morning stiffness.explanation: Stiffness in joints upon waking is common in aging or autoimmune conditions like RA.
morning stiffness.advice:
• Take a warm shower first thing in the morning.
• Gentle bed stretches before standing up.
• Use heat wraps on stiff joints.
